input.strategy_title: Graduate Llama Stack to General Availability
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Llama Stack shipped as Tech Preview and adoption is strong, but enterprise
customers will not build production GenAI applications on a TP component.
Graduating to GA requires API stability commitments, a production support
posture, and closing the quality gaps that TP status currently excuses. The
full inventory of those gaps is not yet known — TP feedback is scattered across
support tickets, and no systematic GA-readiness assessment has been done.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | A GA-readiness assessment inventories the gaps between current TP quality and GA bar (API stability, upgrade paths, scale limits, error handling), producing the definitive GA scope. |
| HLR-2 | P0 | Published API surface carries a stability guarantee: versioned APIs, deprecation policy, and a tested upgrade path from the last two TP releases. |
| HLR-3 | P0 | Production support posture is in place: documented SLO targets, backport policy, and supported configuration matrix. |
| HLR-4 | P1 | Safety guardrails via TrustyAI are a supported, documented integration (not an experimental flag) for GA distributions. |
| HLR-5 | P1 | The Dashboard enables Llama Stack management by default for entitled clusters (no TP opt-in gate). |
| HLR-6 | P2 | Documentation is uplifted to GA standards, including migration notes from TP. |

## Affected Components

- Llama Stack
- TrustyAI
- Dashboard

## Out of Scope

- New Llama Stack feature development beyond GA-bar quality work
- Deprecating alternative GenAI serving paths

## Open Questions

1. The GA scope itself depends on HLR-1's assessment — until it lands, the
   size of the stability and hardening work is an estimate.

# GA-readiness assessment for Llama Stack

## Description

This epic resolves the strategy's defining unknown: no systematic GA-readiness
assessment of Llama Stack has been done, and TP-era feedback is scattered
across support tickets. The epic produces the definitive GA-readiness
assessment — a gap inventory across the four categories named by the strategy
(API stability, upgrade paths, scale limits, error handling) — comparing
current Tech Preview quality against the GA bar. Its output is the definitive
GA scope that the stability and hardening implementation work is sized and
shaped against.

## Scope

- Aggregate and systematically review TP feedback from support tickets, mapped
  to gap items in the assessment.
- Assess current API stability against GA requirements (surface inventory,
  versioning state, breaking-change exposure).
- Assess upgrade paths from recent TP releases (what breaks, what is untested).
- Assess scale limits (documented vs. actual, untested ranges).
- Assess error handling quality against GA expectations.
- For each gap: severity, proposed remediation, and size estimate.
- Produce the definitive GA scope document, ratified by product and support
  stakeholders as the commitment baseline for graduation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A written GA-readiness assessment exists covering all four gap categories
  (API stability, upgrade paths, scale limits, error handling), each with
  current state, GA bar, and identified gaps.
- Every identified gap item is enumerated with a severity, a proposed
  remediation, and a size estimate.
- TP feedback from support tickets has been systematically reviewed and each
  relevant item is traceable to a gap entry in the assessment (or explicitly
  dispositioned as out of scope).
- The assessment is published and accepted by the strategy owner as the
  definitive GA scope for graduation.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-1 (P0)**: GA-readiness assessment inventories the gaps between current
  TP quality and GA bar, producing the definitive GA scope — this epic is the
  assessment itself.

# Close inventoried GA gaps in Llama Stack

## Description

This epic closes the quality gaps that the GA-readiness assessment inventories
between current Tech Preview quality and the GA bar — the remediation work
that TP status currently excuses. Its contents are defined by the assessment's
findings (expected to concentrate in error handling, scale limits, and
stability hardening), which is why it cannot be sized or started before the
assessment lands.

## Scope

- Remediate every gap item the GA-readiness assessment marks as blocking GA,
  following each item's proposed remediation.
- Error-handling gaps: bring error behavior in the identified surfaces up to
  the GA bar defined by the assessment.
- Scale-limit gaps: close identified scale deficiencies and validate the
  documented scale limits.
- Stability hardening items surfaced by the assessment beyond the named API
  stability deliverables.
- Each remediation carries a test demonstrating the gap is closed against the
  assessment's pass criteria.
- Re-run the failing items from the assessment's gap inventory to record
  closure.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every gap item the GA-readiness assessment marks as GA-blocking is
  remediated, and each remediation passes the assessment's own pass criterion
  for that item.
- Error-handling and scale-limit gaps identified by the assessment are closed
  and verified by the tests attached to their remediations.
- The updated gap inventory records every item as closed (or explicitly
  re-scoped with stakeholder sign-off recorded in the assessment document).
- The existing build pipeline for the Llama Stack midstream repository remains
  green for all changes introduced by this epic.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-1 (P0)**: GA-readiness assessment producing the definitive GA scope —
  this epic delivers the gap-closure half of that requirement (the assessment
  identifies the scope; this epic closes it to the GA bar).

## Risks / Notes

- Sizing is an estimate until the GA-readiness assessment lands; if the
  assessment finds the gap set larger than estimated, the additional
  remediation items are absorbed here or split out by sub-system at that
  point.

# API stability guarantee and tested upgrade path

## Description

This epic puts a stability guarantee on Llama Stack's published API surface so
enterprise customers can build production GenAI applications against it: the
API surface is versioned, a deprecation policy is published and applied, and a
tested upgrade path from the last two TP releases is delivered. This is the
core GA commitment named by HLR-2.

## Scope

- Version the published API surface (the OpenAI-compatible REST APIs and the
  LlamaStackDistribution CRD surface) per the platform's versioning approach.
- Author and publish a deprecation policy for the API surface, consistent with
  the GA stability guarantee.
- Apply the deprecation policy: any API slated for removal or change is marked
  and communicated per the policy rather than silently broken.
- Build and test the upgrade path from the last two TP releases, including a
  documented upgrade procedure.
- Adjust scope to any API-stability or upgrade-path findings from the
  GA-readiness assessment (the assessment's findings on these categories
  define the full extent of hardening this surface needs).

## Acceptance Criteria

- The published API surface is versioned and the versioning is documented.
- A deprecation policy is published, and every deprecated or changed API on
  the surface is marked and communicated per that policy.
- The upgrade path from each of the last two TP releases is exercised by an
  automated test and passes, with a documented upgrade procedure.
- A published API stability guarantee statement covers the versioned surface.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-2 (P0)**: Published API surface carries a stability guarantee —
  versioned APIs, deprecation policy, and a tested upgrade path from the last
  two TP releases — this epic delivers that requirement in full.

## Risks / Notes

- The published REST API surface originates upstream; aligning versioning and
  deprecation semantics may require coordination with the upstream project,
  which could extend the timeline.
- Per the strategy's open question, the size of the stability work is an
  estimate until the GA-readiness assessment lands; this epic is gated on that
  assessment and its scope may be rewritten by its findings.

# Production support posture for Llama Stack GA

## Description

This epic establishes the production support posture required for GA:
documented SLO targets, a backport policy, and a supported configuration
matrix. These deliverables are defined by the strategy independent of the
GA-readiness assessment's findings, so the work proceeds in parallel with the
assessment and hardening rather than being gated by them.

## Scope

- Define and document SLO targets for the GA component (availability and
  operational targets appropriate to a GA GenAI API layer).
- Define and document a backport policy (which release lines receive fixes,
  and for how long).
- Define and document the supported configuration matrix: the distributions,
  providers, versions, and scale ranges Red Hat supports at GA.
- Reflect in the configuration matrix only configurations validated during
  the GA stability, upgrade, and hardening work — the matrix must not claim
  support for unvalidated configurations.
- Secure review and sign-off of the support posture from the accountable
  support and product stakeholders.

## Acceptance Criteria

- SLO targets for the GA component are documented and reviewed by the
  accountable support stakeholders.
- The backport policy is documented and reviewed by the accountable support
  stakeholders.
- The supported configuration matrix is documented, and every entry in it
  corresponds to a configuration validated by the GA stability, upgrade-path,
  or hardening work (no unvalidated claims).
- The support posture documentation is accepted as the production support
  basis for the GA release.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-3 (P0)**: Production support posture is in place — documented SLO
  targets, backport policy, and supported configuration matrix — this epic
    delivers that requirement in full.

## Risks / Notes

- The supported configuration matrix's final content depends on the limits
  and configurations validated by the parallel stability and hardening work;
  finalize the matrix after those validations complete (an acceptance-criterion
  gate, not a start-order dependency).
- SLO targets and the backport policy require support/product sign-off — a
  human process gate that may add elapsed time beyond the engineering work.

# Supported TrustyAI guardrails integration for GA distributions

## Description

This epic makes the TrustyAI safety-guardrails integration with Llama Stack
distributions a supported, documented integration for GA — promoted from the
experimental flag it ships as today. The integration itself already exists
experimentally; this epic delivers the validation, testing, and documentation
that "supported" requires, targeted at the versioned, stability-guaranteed GA
API surface.

## Scope

- Promote the guardrails integration from an experimental flag to a supported
  configuration path for GA Llama Stack distributions.
- Validate the integration against the versioned GA API surface (the
  stability-guaranteed surface, not the TP-era surface the experimental
  integration was wired against).
- Define and test the supported integration configurations (which TrustyAI
  service versions with which distribution configurations are supported).
- Validate and document fail-mode behavior: what happens to requests and
  distributions when the guardrails service is unavailable or degraded, and
  what the operator/administrator recovery path is.
- Document the integration for GA distributions: enablement, supported
  configurations, and failure behavior.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The guardrails integration is enabled through a supported configuration
  path — no experimental flag is required for GA distributions.
- The integration is validated by automated tests against the versioned GA
  API surface, and those tests pass.
- The supported integration configurations are enumerated and each is covered
  by a passing test.
- Fail-mode behavior of the integration (guardrails service unavailable or
  degraded) is tested and documented, including the recovery path.
- Integration documentation suitable for GA distributions is published
  (enablement, supported configurations, failure behavior).

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-4 (P1)**: Safety guardrails via TrustyAI are a supported, documented
  integration (not an experimental flag) for GA distributions — this epic
  delivers that requirement in full.

## Risks / Notes

- This epic's work spans two components: the TrustyAI service side (owned by
  the TrustyAI team) and the Llama Stack distribution wiring; the single
  most-relevant component is TrustyAI, and cross-team coordination with the
  Llama Stack distribution work is required.
- The integration must build against the stability-guaranteed API surface, so
  this work serializes after the API stability work; starting earlier would
  validate against a surface that may still change.

# Dashboard Llama Stack management on by default for entitled clusters

## Description

This epic enables Llama Stack management in the Dashboard by default for
entitled clusters, removing the Tech Preview opt-in gate. The management
surface already exists behind an opt-in flag; this epic changes the default
so entitled clusters get Llama Stack management without action.

## Scope

- Change the Dashboard's per-component feature-flag default so Llama Stack
  management is enabled by default for entitled clusters, delivered through
  the Dashboard's existing feature-flag and defaults mechanism.
- Remove the Tech Preview opt-in gate for Llama Stack management.
- Preserve entitlement behavior: clusters without the relevant entitlement do
  not get Llama Stack management enabled.
- Provide a configuration path to disable the default (rollback/override).
- Update captions, labels, and references that fall out of this change (e.g.
  TP labeling on the Llama Stack management section) — incidental touch-ups
  only, no new content.

## Acceptance Criteria

- On an entitled cluster, Llama Stack management is available in the Dashboard
  with no opt-in configuration change required.
- On a cluster without the relevant entitlement, Llama Stack management is not
  enabled.
- The default can be reverted or overridden through configuration, and that
  override path is tested.
- The existing Dashboard test suite passes, with tests updated to cover the
  new default behavior.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-5 (P1)**: The Dashboard enables Llama Stack management by default for
  entitled clusters (no TP opt-in gate) — this epic delivers that requirement
  in full.

# GA-standard documentation uplift with TP migration notes

## Description

This epic uplifts Llama Stack documentation to GA standards, including
migration notes from Tech Preview. It runs last: the documentation describes
what was actually built — the stabilized APIs, the support posture, the
supported guardrails integration, the default Dashboard enablement, and the
remediated quality gaps — so it is blocked by all implementation work in this
strategy.

## Scope

Content outline:

- GA overview of Llama Stack: what is supported at GA, component positioning,
  and the supported deployment model.
- API stability documentation: the versioned API surface, the stability
  guarantee, and the deprecation policy.
- Migration notes from Tech Preview: how to move from the last two TP
  releases to GA, following the tested upgrade path.
- Support posture documentation: SLO targets, backport policy, and the
  supported configuration matrix.
- The supported TrustyAI guardrails integration: enablement, supported
  configurations, and failure behavior for GA distributions.
- Dashboard enablement: Llama Stack management on entitled clusters by
  default, including how to override the default.
- Removal/revision of Tech Preview framing: caveats, disclaimers, and
  experimental flags documentation that GA status supersedes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- GA-standard documentation is published covering every topic in the scope
  outline.
- Migration notes from Tech Preview are included and walk through the upgrade
  from each of the last two TP releases.
- All documentation is technically reviewed against the implemented GA
  behavior (reviewed by the engineering owners of the documented surfaces),
  with review sign-off recorded.
- No documentation remains that frames Llama Stack as Tech Preview or
  experimental where GA support supersedes it.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-6 (P2)**: Documentation is uplifted to GA standards, including
  migration notes from TP — this epic delivers that requirement in full.
